\begin{restated}{Remark}{rem:B3-fixed-step}{B3}{0}{the step is fixed in advance}
One may not replace $R^2$ by $\LEff(t-1)$ inside $\gamma$: the step was chosen before the trajectory was observed, and $\Delta=3\gamma^2$ with it. With $\gamma=\frac1{4R^2}$ fixed, a smaller effective smoothness $\LEff<R^2$ enters only through the bracket $1-\frac{5\LEff}{8R^2}\in[\frac38,1)$: the gain from (I2) being loose is at most a factor $\frac83$ on the parameter rate. By contrast $\muEff(t-1)$ enters linearly and may exceed $\mu$ by orders of magnitude (for logistic regression, $\mu=\lambda$ while $\muEff(\theta)$ is $\lambda$ plus the curvature of the data term in the direction $\theta-\etastar$, averaged along the segment $[\etastar,\theta]$; see the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:B3-logistic}), which is why hypothesis (B2) focuses on $\muEff$. A step adapted to $\LEff$ would be a different algorithm, and $\Delta$ would have to follow $\gamma$; see also the discussion of step-size selection in \cite[Sec.~3.A]{gower2020variance}.
\end{restated}
